blocks.text: # Results Matrix and Interpretation Guide
## Review state
Draft for user review. Every cell below is a planned result slot; no empirical value has been entered or inferred.
## What the paper must distinguish
The study has three different questions. They should not be collapsed into one leaderboard number.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  A["Is the handoff representation itself causal?\nIsolated receiver"] --> B["Does it help a real multi-stage workflow?\nFixed M0 end-to-end"]
  B --> C["Does the effect depend on model family?\nTwo-arm model sweep"]
```
## Matrix A: isolated handoff diagnostic
This is a single-edge experiment. The upstream artifact and public workspace are identical; only the materialized history changes.

| Dimension | Fixed | Varied |
|---|---|---|
| Task | 2 frozen Harvey tasks | task instance |
| Handoff boundary | `V1 → V2`, `V2 → V3` | boundary |
| Upstream content | canonical evidence map / decision register | never varies inside a pair |
| Receiver | fresh session, same role, same M0 model and effort | three independent attempts |
| Arm | same current artifact and token budget | `mas-memory`, `mas-proofpress-lineage` |
Planned cells: `2 tasks × 2 boundaries × 2 arms × 3 attempts = 24` receiver-only calls.

Primary measurements: decision recovery accuracy, decision regression, unsupported authority upgrade, correct reversal, false block, input tokens, latency, tool calls/history reads. Its value is causal clarity: if Proofpress changes an outcome here, the difference cannot be blamed on upstream agents having produced different artifacts.
## Matrix B: fixed-model end-to-end workflow
This is the primary systems experiment. All agents in a row use the same exact M0 model configuration and `high` effort.

| Arm | 6 tasks × 5 attempts | Role in interpretation |
|---|---:|---|
| `single-agent` | 30 workflows | decomposition reference |
| `mas-artifact` | 30 workflows | latest-artifact reference |
| `mas-memory` | 30 workflows | **primary ordinary-memory control** |
| `mas-memory-chain` | 30 workflows | raw-history comparator |
| `mas-proofpress-lineage` | 30 workflows | **primary treatment** |
Total: `6 × 5 × 5 = 150` workflows. It is launched only after Gate 1 passes and in reviewable task blocks, not as one blind batch.

Unlike Matrix A, rows can diverge after the first receiver. That is intentional: this matrix measures the accumulated system consequence of carrying one representation throughout a real V0–V4 workflow. It cannot by itself prove that every later edge received identical upstream content; Matrix A supplies that mechanism evidence.
For each cell, report:

| Quality | Trust | Efficiency | Integrity |
|---|---|---|---|
| official Harvey rubric and `trusted_task_success` | regression, unsupported upgrade, correct reversal, false block | input/output tokens, latency, cost, tools, history reads | capsule verification, artifact continuity, declared actor/status agreement |
## Matrix C: cross-model replication
Keep the harness and workflow fixed. Change the entire homogeneous team together; do not use a costly coordinator paired with cheap workers in the core causal matrix.

| Candidate team | Primary arms | Tasks | Attempts | Interpretation |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| frozen M0 reference | memory, Proofpress | 3–4 | 3 | anchor / replication |
| Claude/OpenAI/frontier candidates | memory, Proofpress | 3–4 | 3 | closed-model family interaction |
| DeepSeek V4 Flash (High), Qwen 3.8, Muse Spark 1.2 | memory, Proofpress | 3–4 | 3 | accessible/open-weight-adjacent family interaction |
| other frozen candidates | memory, Proofpress | 3–4 | 3 | only if API/tool contract and cost are stable |

Each row is an exact concrete OpenRouter slug with a provider-routing freeze and resolved response metadata. Candidate selection may use the Agent Arena leaderboard as a sampling signal, but the paper does not treat that leaderboard as legal-work validation.
The maximum is `10 teams × 2 arms × 4 tasks × 3 attempts = 240` workflows. A smaller sweep is scientifically preferable to a large, under-audited grid.
## The result table that should appear in the paper
The main table should use a difference relative to the primary memory control, not only an absolute score.

| Model team | Arm | Trusted success | Official score | Regression / upgrade | Correct reversal | Input tokens | Latency | Cost | Tool/history work |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| M0 | memory | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … |
| M0 | Proofpress | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … |
| M0 | **PP − memory** | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … |
| M1 | memory | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … |
| M1 | Proofpress | … | … | … | … | … | … | … | … |

Put Matrix B's `single-agent`, artifact, and memory-chain references in a companion table. Show task-level dot plots and per-model differences beside aggregates; do not hide a heterogenous outcome under a single mean.
## Interpretation rules

| Observed pattern | Responsible statement |
|---|---|
| Proofpress improves isolated recovery and end-to-end trusted success versus strong memory, without reversal harm | Evidence supports a bounded provenance-handoff mechanism for the frozen tasks/workflow/model(s). |
| Proofpress wins only against latest artifact, not strong memory | Claim ordinary handoff memory matters; do not claim a distinctive Proofpress benefit. |
| Proofpress matches memory but uses fewer tokens/latency/history reads | Claim an efficiency or auditability advantage only if task/trust quality is not materially worse. |
| Proofpress is worse at justified reversal or causes false blocks | The preservation framing failed on adaptive decision-making; report it and revise the protocol. |
| Effect appears only in one model team | State a model interaction, not a general provenance effect. |
| Controls lack the intended recovery error | Stop or redesign; a scaled matrix would not test the proposed mechanism. |
## What is not a valid conclusion

- A higher Harvey rubric alone does not prove preserved trust.
- A model sweep does not compare harnesses.
- A raw-history win does not imply that more context is intrinsically better; it may only expose a missing ordinary-memory control.
- An ARA trace or a valid Proofpress capsule does not certify legal correctness; it records research/artifact provenance at different layers.
